name: COVUnity Fridge — Redden Gardens
address: Doc John Redden Way, 909 Scott Blvd, Covington, KY 41011
limitations: Public operator website information and linked photographs; no on-site audit. This listing covers Redden Gardens, not the separate Banklick Street fridge. The service is self-serve with no staff present; door effort, shelf and control reach, pavement/threshold dimensions, continuous parking-to-fridge access, seating and toilets/changing facilities remain unverified. Food and supply stocks and equipment operation can change; the website is not a live inventory or a food-safety inspection. Photo dates are unknown.
facts: The Redden Gardens fridge is listed on Doc John Redden Way at 909 Scott Boulevard. COVUnity describes its Covington fridges as free, open every day around the clock, and self-serve with no staff present.
Two free spots in Covington, open day and night. Anyone can donate or take. Swing by whenever it suits you. There is no staff present and no schedule to keep because it is self-serve.
Open 24/7 · every day of the year
Doc John Redden Way 909 Scott Blvd Covington, KY 41011
COVUnity says anyone may take food without signing in or explaining their need. No sign-up, cost or questions are required; the site does not establish assisted shopping or delivery.
The COVUnity Fridge is Covington's free community fridge and pantry. Two locations, stocked by neighbors and open around the clock. If you need food, it's yours. No sign-up, no questions.
Hungry, stretched thin, or just passing by? Help yourself. It's free and open to everyone, and nobody's going to ask you to sign in or explain why you're there.

The operator lists refrigerated and frozen food, a microwave and a hot/cold water station at Redden Gardens. These are published amenities, not confirmation that equipment is working or stocked at the time of a visit.
The main fridge, with refrigerated and frozen food, a microwave, and a hot & cold water station.

The operator asks visitors to shut the fridge door tightly, wipe spills and discard items past their prime. Donations must exclude opened or expired food and unlabeled prepared or home-cooked food; labeled meals from commercial kitchens are accepted. Individual food suitability is not established.
Wipe up spills, toss anything past its prime, and shut the door tight. A few seconds of care keeps the next person's food safe and the fridge worth coming back to.
Labeled meals from a commercial kitchen

A free NKY Health wellness kiosk is described immediately to the left of the main Redden Gardens fridge, open around the clock without sign-up. Supplies may vary. The source does not describe the approach, door controls or reach to its compartments.

The Northern Kentucky Health Department installed a free, judgment-free wellness kiosk immediately to the left of the main fridge at Redden Gardens. Like the fridge, it is open to everyone around the clock: take what you need, no sign-up and no questions. It is stocked with lifesaving and everyday health and safety supplies.

COVUnity describes the fridge as supplemental food support and directs people needing recurring help to established social services. It says it has no staff and relies on community helpers, so prompt personal assistance is not assured.
We recognize we are not solving hunger alone. We rely on established social services to help meet ongoing need, and we are supplemental to these resources.

If you are in need of recurring help, please reach out to these services. Be Concerned, for example, offers monthly pantry registration, emergency food assistance, mobile pantry support, and homebound delivery. The direct links below can take you straight to local pantries, churches, and assistance programs.

Send us a message with an open question. Want to pitch in, drop off a donation, ask about an item request, or find out about starting a fridge where you live? We do not have staff, so we rely on helpers in the community, but we'll get back to you when we can.
